title: Col. John Bowman at Old Chillicothe
summary: In May 1779 Col. John Bowman led Kentucky militia against the Shawnee town of Old Chillicothe in Ohio, burning cabins but failing to take the blockhouse.
bodyMarkdown:
Colonel John Bowman led a 1779 raid north of the Ohio River against the Shawnee town of Old Chillicothe. Kentucky settlers called it a victory. For the Shawnee it meant a burned town and the loss of their war chief Blackfish.

## The colonel

[John Bowman](https://grokipedia.com/page/john_bowman_(pioneer)) says he was born in 1738 on Cedar Creek in Virginia's Shenandoah Valley, a grandson of the pioneer Jost Hite. He and his brothers, including [Joseph Bowman](/stories/maj-joseph-bowman/), were among Kentucky's earliest settler officers. He fought at Point Pleasant in 1774.

Bowman served on the Harrodsburg safety committee in 1776. He became the first county lieutenant of Kentucky County that year and arrived at Harrodsburg that September with two companies of about 100 men.

## The raid of May 1779

After [George Rogers Clark](/stories/george-rogers-clark/) took Kaskaskia, he asked Bowman for men for a planned move on Detroit. Bowman promised at least 300 and gathered men and supplies that spring.

[The Battle of Chillicothe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Chillicothe) says Bowman, joined by [Benjamin Logan](/stories/benjamin-logan/) and [Levi Todd](/stories/levi-todd-lexington-co-founder/), led between 160 and 300 militiamen against Old Chillicothe on May 29. They split their force and attacked from two sides but were driven back. The Shawnee held out in a single blockhouse.

Bowman burned much of the town and withdrew with 163 horses valued at $32,000. The Shawnee pursued as the militia marched south. One account reports 8 militiamen killed and 4 wounded, and about 4 or 5 Shawnee killed.

## Blackfish and the verdict

[Blackfish](/stories/blackfish-cot-ta-wa-ma-go-chillicothe-war-chief/), the town's war leader, died of his wounds. Bowman and Logan were first blamed for failing to take the blockhouse and for their losses. Later the raid was credited as a major Kentucky victory that discouraged further war parties. Theodore Roosevelt wrote that it "undoubtedly accomplished more than Clark's attack on Piqua next year."

That judgment comes from the settlers' side. For the Shawnee of Chillicothe, the raid meant a burned town, lost horses and a dead leader in the midst of their war against settler expansion into Kentucky.

## Later years

That fall Bowman and his brother Abraham founded Bowman's Station on Cane Run in present Mercer County. In 1781 he became the first sheriff and county lieutenant of Lincoln County and presided over the first county court held in Kentucky. He died at his home in May 1784.

## Kentucky today

Bowman's Station stood near present Burgin in Mercer County. It says the brick mansion his son built, Mt. Pleasant, still stands near the old station site. Old Chillicothe lay north of the Ohio River in present-day Ohio, and the raid remains a central episode in accounts of Kentucky's Revolutionary frontier.
